To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully fabricated flexible gas sensors using a simple method for transfer of CNTs from SiO2/SI substrate to flexible substrate and the gas sensor exhibited high sensitivity for CO2 NH3 and isopropyle alcohol gas sensing at the room temperature.

we have developed a new approach that allows for the transfer of CNT films from a SiO/Si substrate to flexible substrates, which is an important step toward the development of low cost, flexible gas sensing devices.

we have developed a simple method to transfer a dense network of CNTs from the SiO2/Silicon substrate to flexible substrates and demonstrated their use for room temperature CO2, NH 3, and IPA gas detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of flexible CNT based gas sensing devices for the detection of toxic gases.
the development of a new flexible gas sensor device based on a simple method for transferring high density CNT networks from SiO2/Sisubstrates to flexible polyimide films.
the synthesis and characterization of carbon nanotube thin films functionalized via the loading of gold nanoclusters for flexible gas sensor devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Au modified semicnducting CNT thin film based chemiresistor exhibits high sensitivities to ambient CO2, isopropyl alcoho, and NH3 gas concentrations.
the CNTs based flexible gas sensor devices are highly promising for the detection of various toxic and flammable gases.
CNT thin films functionalized via loading of Au nanoclusters are promising for the fabrication of flexible gas sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Au modified CNT thin films have been successfully transferred to a flexible substrate, which could be a potential candidate for flexible gas sensor devices.
CNTs are a very promising material for the development of low-cost flexible gas sensing devices.
we developed a new method to fabricate flexible CNT thin film sensors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simple method for the transfer of CNT thin film from Si substrate to flexible substrate and the use of Au nanoclusters for gas sensing can be applied to a wide range of flexible devices.
the simple transfer of CNT thin films to flexible substrates can provide a viable path to low cost flexible gas sensing devices.
the CNT based sensor can be fabricated at low cost and with simple methods.
